theme: Incentive travel as a retention tool, not a reward

linkedin.text:
Incentive travel gets mislabeled as a reward program. The companies seeing real ROI treat it as something else entirely: a retention and culture investment.

Here's the distinction that matters in practice:

A reward says "you did well."
An incentive program says "this is what it means to be part of this team."

The experience design — who's in the room, what they access, how the brand shows up in the destination — determines which message your participants actually receive.

Across 130+ destinations and 25,000+ participants, the programs that moved the needle on retention weren't the most expensive. They were the most intentional.

If you're in the early stages of planning an incentive program and want a peer-level conversation about what works, I'm happy to connect. No pitch — just a real conversation.

instagram.text:
A flight and a hotel room is a trip.

Access, meaning, and a shared memory that your team talks about a year later — that's an incentive program.

We've built both. One drives bookings. The other drives retention.

After 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, the difference is always in the design — not the destination.

facebook.text:
The best incentive trips don't feel like a prize. They feel like belonging.

When your top performers land in a destination they've never seen, get access no one else gets, and share something genuinely unforgettable with their team — that's not a perk. That's a retention strategy.

We've run incentive programs across 130+ destinations for 25,000+ participants. The companies that do this well aren't throwing money at travel. They're building loyalty that outlasts any counter-offer.
